slides.title: A signed directory, not a [locked door].
slides.lede: llms.txt can guide AI agents to your best pages. It cannot control access, rankings or citations.

slides.title: A proposal, not a [ratified web standard]
slides.text: Different AI products, crawlers and platforms may ignore it, interpret it differently or never request it at all. Treat it as a useful experiment.

cards.label: Can
cards.text: Offer a compact path to selected, authoritative pages.

cards.label: Cannot
cards.text: Control access, force indexing or guarantee citations.

items.title: A preference note
items.text: Use linked canonical pages for detail.

slides.title: Requests prove [interest], not influence
slides.text: A consultancy seeing 50 requests in a month knows the file was requested. It does not know the file shaped any answer.

slides.title: Update it when [positioning changes]
slides.note: Review at least **quarterly** for stable sites. A stale summary can do more damage than no file.

slides.title: Fix the foundations before the file.
slides.lede: llms.txt for professional services firms: what it does and doesn't do. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
